pairs.question: Quae tandem ista causa est?
pairs.answer: Quia si verum dicimus, haec est mea et huius fratris mei germana patria.
pairs.derivation: Atticus asks for the 'alia causa' Marcus has just mentioned ('me alia quoque causa delectat'); 'ista causa' refers to it. Marcus's reply answers directly; window ends at the first full stop ('germana patria.'), before he turns to elaborating (Hic enim orti stirpe...).

pairs.question: Numquid duas habetis patrias, an est una illa patria communis?
pairs.answer: Ego mehercule et illi et omnibus municipibus duas esse censeo patrias, unam naturae, alteram civitatis.
pairs.derivation: Atticus's double interrogative (numquid... an...) about one vs. two homelands. Marcus answers 'two'; answer cut at 'alteram civitatis' (the colon in the source) where he turns to the Cato example as elaboration. Terminal colon normalized to a full stop.

pairs.question: Quo si civitas careat ob eam ipsam causam quod eo careat pro nihilo habenda sit, id estne numerandum in bonis?
pairs.derivation: Dropped the speech-framing 'Quaero igitur a te Quinte, sicut illi solent:' as a question tag; kept the interrogative (estne...). Quintus answers; first word capitalized.

pairs.question: Lege autem carens civitas estne ob ipsum habenda nullo loco?
pairs.derivation: Marcus's -ne interrogative directly answered by Quintus. No trimming needed.

pairs.question: Video quae sint in pontificio iure, sed quaero ecquidnam sit in legibus.
pairs.answer: Pauca sane Tite, et ut arbitror non ignota vobis.
pairs.derivation: Atticus's indirect interrogative (quaero ecquidnam...) kept whole for the pontifical-vs-statute contrast. Marcus's reply answers 'a few things'; window ends at the first full stop, before he turns to specifics (Sed ea non tam ad religionem...).
